issues.legal_issue: The possession requirement for specific performance of a building contract does not bar a developer with an interest in the property from suing the owner for specific performance.
material_facts: The developer sued the owner for specific performance of a development agreement.

The agreement provided for the developer to construct a building and receive a share of the constructed area, but the Court found that this agreement did not create an interest in the land for the developer.
The owner, as defendant, held possession by virtue of lawful title, rather than having obtained possession under the agreement.
issues.conclusion: Where a developer has an interest in the property, the possession condition is not a bar to the developer’s suit against the owner; the developer must still satisfy the requirements that the work be sufficiently defined and that money compensation be inadequate.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(3)(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits specific performance of certain building contracts when its conditions are met. The Court purposively interpreted Section 14(3)(c)(iii), because a literal reading would anomalously prevent a developer with an interest in the property from suing an owner who remained in possession by lawful title. In doing so, it relied on the principles for departing from statutory text discussed in G.P. Singh’s Principles of Statutory Interpretation, Stock v Frank Jones (Tipton) Ltd. and Maxwell on Interpretation of Statutes. The general requirements for specific performance of a building contract were also discussed with reference to Wolverhampton Corporation v Emmons, Carpenters Estate v Davies, and Price v Strange.

predicates.developer_suit_for_specific_performance: A developer brings a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to develop or build on land.
predicates.developer_has_interest_in_property: The development agreement gives the developer an interest in the land or in rights associated with the land or its development.
predicates.owner_is_defendant: The property owner is the defendant in the developer’s suit.

issues.definition: When a developer with an interest in the property sues its owner for specific performance, the owner’s not having obtained possession under the agreement does not itself bar the suit.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance of a building contract is unavailable when the work is not defined precisely enough for the court to determine its scope and money compensation adequately addresses the claimed loss.
material_facts: The agreement described the proposed building and finishes using vague terms, including references to first-class materials, apartments of various sizes, and other unspecified features.
The agreement did not specify the exact remuneration payable to the developer.
No construction had taken place, and the developer’s claimed expenditure and losses could be quantified and compensated in money.
The developer did not establish the conditions for specific performance concerning sufficiently precise work and an interest for which money compensation was inadequate.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was too vague for the court to determine the exact nature of the work, and the alleged losses could be compensated in money; the conditions for specific performance were not met, so specific performance could not be granted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(3)(c)(i) and (ii) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 require the building or work to be described sufficiently precisely for the court to determine its exact nature, and require the plaintiff to have a substantial interest for which money compensation is not adequate. The Court applied the established requirements for specific performance of a building contract discussed in Wolverhampton Corporation v Emmons, Carpenters Estate v Davies, and Price v Strange. It also treated the terms of the agreement as decisive in determining the nature of the development arrangement and any interest created for the developer.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit_for_building_contract and work_description_is_vague and claimed_loss_is_quantifiable and money_compensation_is_adequate

predicates.specific_performance_suit_for_building_c: A plaintiff seeks specific performance of an agreement to construct a building or perform other work on land.
predicates.work_description_is_vague: The agreement does not define the work precisely enough for a court to determine its exact nature and scope.
predicates.claimed_loss_is_quantifiable: The plaintiff’s alleged losses from non-performance can be calculated in money.
predicates.money_compensation_is_adequate: A monetary award can adequately remedy the plaintiff’s loss from non-performance.

issues.definition: If a plaintiff seeks specific performance of a building contract whose work is insufficiently defined and whose alleged losses can be adequately remedied with money, specific performance cannot be granted.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal need not be remitted for consideration of monetary relief when that relief was not sought and the appellant declined the opportunity to amend the claim to seek it.
material_facts: The first appellate court indicated that the plaintiff could amend the claim to seek return of the security money and damages.
The plaintiff declined that opportunity and maintained the request for specific performance.
The plaintiff made the same position clear before the Supreme Court, and no alternative plea for monetary relief was before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to remit the appeal for consideration of monetary relief because the plaintiff had not sought that relief and had declined the opportunity to amend the claim.
issues.legal_principle: Although an appellate court would ordinarily consider remitting a case where an alternative claim for damages or monetary relief requires consideration, the Court found no basis for remittal in the absence of such a claim, particularly after the plaintiff expressly declined an opportunity to amend. The discussion concerned the proposed alternative relief under Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_specific_performan: An appellant challenges a decision denying specific performance of a contract.
predicates.alternative_monetary_relief_not_claimed: The appellant has not asked the court to grant an alternative monetary remedy.
predicates.appellant_declined_opportunity_to_amend: The appellant declined an opportunity to amend the claim to seek monetary relief.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges denial of specific performance, the appellant has not claimed monetary relief, and the appellant declined an opportunity to add that claim, the appeal need not be remitted to consider monetary relief.
